headline.headline: SPURS TORCH WOLVES BY 30, ADVANCE TO CONFERENCE FINALS WITH DOMINANT 139-109 DEMOLITION
headline.deck: San Antonio's offensive explosion sends Minnesota packing as Spurs roll into the final four.
headline.body:
SAN ANTONIO — The Minnesota Timberwolves arrived for Friday night's second-round elimination game with playoff experience and home-court memory. They left with nothing but a 30-point loss and an early summer. The San Antonio Spurs detonated for 139 points in a 139-109 rout that was as complete and authoritative a playoff performance as the Western Conference has seen in years, punching their ticket to the conference finals with a performance that silenced every doubter who questioned whether this young Spurs core was built for May basketball.

San Antonio's offense operated like a well-oiled machine from the opening tip, exploiting Minnesota's perimeter defense at will and getting to the free-throw line with alarming regularity. The Spurs' ball movement sliced apart a Timberwolves scheme that had carried Minnesota through the first round, and by the time the third quarter arrived, the outcome was a formality. The 30-point margin marked one of the most lopsided second-round clinching victories in recent postseason memory.

The result sets up a conference finals matchup with potentially seismic implications for the Western Conference pecking order. San Antonio, written off by many analysts before the postseason began, has now dispatched Minnesota in convincing fashion and enters the next round with momentum, health, and the kind of collective confidence that is genuinely difficult to manufacture. The Spurs will await their opponent while the rest of the league recalibrates its championship math accordingly.

secondary.headline: GAME 7 SUNDAY: BERENSON BOWL RELOADED AS PISTONS, CAVS GO TO THE WIRE
secondary.deck: Detroit's 115-94 blowout Friday forces a winner-take-all showdown in the Motor City.
secondary.body:
DETROIT — The Cleveland Cavaliers entered Friday with a chance to close out the series and advance to the Eastern Conference finals. Instead, the Detroit Pistons handed them a 115-94 thrashing that felt more like a statement than a basketball game, forcing a Game 7 Sunday at Little Caesars Arena. The Pistons, listed as 30-to-1 longshots to win the NBA championship before the postseason began, have now turned what looked like a short series into one of the conference semifinals' most compelling storylines.

Detroit's defense suffocated Cleveland's usually reliable half-court offense while the Pistons' transition game produced easy baskets in bunches. Sunday's Game 7 will be the fifth time these two franchises have met in a deciding game since 2006, and both clubs carry storied memories from those occasions. One of them ends its season on Sunday. The winner earns the right to face whichever team emerges from the Atlantic Division bracket, with the Eastern Conference finals picture coming sharply into focus.

secondary.headline: BERRIOS ELBOW SURGERY CLOUDS TORONTO'S ROTATION FUTURE
secondary.deck: Blue Jays ace heads to the operating table Wednesday with no timetable for return.
secondary.body:
TORONTO — The Toronto Blue Jays absorbed another blow to their already battered pitching staff Friday when the club confirmed right-hander Jose Berrios will undergo elbow surgery Wednesday. No recovery timeline will be known until doctors complete the procedure and assess the damage, leaving Toronto's front office to navigate a rotation crisis with no clear end date. The Blue Jays also dropped a 3-2 decision to the Detroit Tigers on Friday, a defeat that stings considerably more given the news surrounding their veteran starter.

Berrios, a two-time All-Star who had been relied upon as a stabilizing force atop Toronto's rotation, represents a significant loss in both innings and leadership. The Blue Jays have already shuffled their pitching staff repeatedly this season and now face the prospect of a prolonged absence from one of their highest-paid arms. Toronto's front office will need to explore trade and waiver options immediately if the club intends to stay relevant in the American League East race through the summer months.

secondary.headline: CANADIENS ONE WIN FROM HURRICANES DATE AS SECOND ROUND NEARS CLIMAX
secondary.deck: Montreal eyes series close Saturday while Carolina watches and waits in the wings.
secondary.body:
MONTREAL — The Montreal Canadiens carry a series lead into Saturday with a chance to clinch and move on to face the Carolina Hurricanes, who have been sitting idle watching the bracket unfold in their favor. The Hurricanes, one of three clubs listed among the Stanley Cup favorites alongside the Colorado Avalanche and Vegas Golden Knights, have been waiting for a conference finals opponent while the Canadiens methodically worked through their second-round series. A Montreal victory Saturday would set up what figures to be a bruising, high-speed matchup between two of the Eastern Conference's most defensively sound programs.

Meanwhile, at the world championships in Europe, San Jose Sharks prospect Macklin Celebrini delivered a reminder of his elite ceiling, scoring twice and adding an assist as Canada rolled to a 6-0 shutout of Italy. Celebrini's performance will do little to reduce the anticipation surrounding his future at the NHL level, though the immediate focus for hockey fans stateside remains the Stanley Cup bracket, which is narrowing quickly toward what promises to be a compelling final four.

column.headline: THE SPURS ARE NO FLUKE, AND EVERYONE KNOWS IT NOW
column.body:
There is a moment in every surprising postseason run when the word surprising stops applying. For the San Antonio Spurs, that moment arrived Friday night at 139 points scored, 30 points of margin, and a Minnesota Timberwolves team walking off the court with absolutely nothing to say. This is not a Cinderella story anymore. This is a legitimate contender, and the rest of the league had better start treating it that way. Thirty-to-one odds to win the title looked reasonable in October. They look almost comical now.

What makes San Antonio genuinely dangerous is not one signature player carrying the load on any given night but rather the collective coherence of a group that plays with a purpose and a pace that opponents simply cannot match over four quarters. The Pistons showed Friday that Detroit is also capable of rising to this level, and a Game 7 Sunday will clarify the Eastern picture. But make no mistake: the story of these playoffs, the thread that will define the conference finals and possibly the championship, runs straight through San Antonio. The Spurs are here. They mean business. Dismiss them at your own peril.

story.headline: PHILLIES OUTLAST PIRATES IN HIGH-OCTANE 11-9 SLUGFEST AT CITIZEN BANK PARK
story.deck: Philadelphia's bats erupt for 11 runs to hold off a furious Pittsburgh rally
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Phillies turned Citizens Bank Park into a fireworks show Friday night, pounding out 11 runs against a Pittsburgh Pirates staff that had no answer for Philadelphia's relentless lineup, then surviving a white-knuckle Pirates comeback attempt to walk away with an 11-9 victory that left the sellout crowd breathless.

The Phillies seized control early, sending multiple batters around the bases in a series of crooked-number innings that gave Philadelphia a cushion that looked comfortable until Pittsburgh clawed back with a furious run in the late innings. The Pirates, refusing to go quietly, strung together hits and drew walks to make a genuine contest of what had appeared to be a Phillies romp, cutting the deficit to two runs before Philadelphia's bullpen finally slammed the door.

The victory keeps the Phillies rolling at a torrid pace in the National League East, where every win carries extra weight this time of year. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, dropped a gut-punch road loss that erases whatever momentum the club had hoped to build heading into the weekend. The two clubs wrap up their brief series Saturday afternoon under clear skies forecast for South Philadelphia.

story.headline: PISTONS STEAMROLL CAVS, FORCE GAME 7 SHOWDOWN IN DETROIT
story.deck: Detroit's blowout win sets up winner-take-all Game 7 for an Eastern Conference Finals berth.
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The Detroit Pistons came into Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse and delivered a statement, dismantling the Cleveland Cavaliers 115-94 Friday night to force a decisive Game 7 and send a jolt of electricity through a franchise that has spent years searching for its identity. Detroit controlled the game from the opening tip, building a lead that never felt threatened and silencing a Cleveland crowd that had expected a close-out performance from the home team.

The Cavaliers, who entered the night needing just one win to advance, looked tentative and disjointed against a Pistons defense that suffocated their half-court sets and turned the game into a track meet on Detroit's terms. Cleveland's offense, so reliable through stretches of this series, found no rhythm against Detroit's length and physicality. The 21-point margin told the full story of a night when the Cavaliers simply had no answer.

In San Antonio, the Spurs rolled past the Minnesota Timberwolves 139-109 in Game 6 to eliminate Anthony Edwards and his squad in stunning fashion. Edwards, visibly drained after the blowout, walked to the Spurs bench to offer his respects as the final seconds ticked away — a somber image capping a Wolves season that ends far short of expectations. The Spurs now await either the Pistons or Cavaliers, with Game 7 set for Sunday.

story.headline: CELEBRINI SHINES AT WORLDS AS CANADIENS CLOSE IN ON HURRICANES SERIES
story.deck: Canada's top prospect dominates in Europe while Montreal eyes a sweep in Buffalo.
story.body:
Macklin Celebrini reminded the hockey world exactly why the San Jose Sharks made him the first overall pick in 2024, scoring twice and adding an assist Friday as Canada rolled to a 6-0 shutout of Italy at the World Championship in Sweden. The 18-year-old center, already drawing comparisons to franchise cornerstones, has Canada sitting at 2-0 in pool play and looking like a gold-medal contender before the tournament hits its second week.

Back on North American ice, the NHL playoffs are hurtling toward a pivotal weekend. The Montreal Canadiens, heavy favorites according to the latest Stanley Cup odds, can close out their first-round series against the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday. The Carolina Hurricanes, listed among the top three Cup favorites alongside the Colorado Avalanche and Vegas Golden Knights, are watching the series closely, waiting to learn which opponent they will face in the next round.

Meanwhile, a sobering injury report out of Minnesota added context to the Wild's second-round exit against Colorado. Defenseman Jonas Brodin and center Joel Eriksson Ek both played through broken bones in their feet during the series, the team confirmed Saturday. The revelation stunned the hockey community and raised pointed questions about how Minnesota might have fared against the Avalanche at full strength, with both players considered cornerstones of the franchise's defensive identity.

story.headline: DRAFT GOLD OR FOOL'S GOLD? TEAMS SCRAMBLE TO EVALUATE APRIL'S ROOKIE CLASS
story.deck: Front offices across the league size up new additions as minicamp season gets underway.
story.body:
With minicamps opening across the league this week, NFL front offices are getting their first live looks at the 2026 draft class, and early returns are drawing both excitement and skepticism. The Cleveland Browns, who traded up to select Tennessee quarterback Marcus Holt with the fifth overall pick, have been generating considerable buzz after Holt impressed coaches with his arm strength and command of the playbook during organized team activities. General manager Andrew Berry called the early workouts "exactly what we hoped to see," though veterans around the league are quick to note that OTAs rarely predict regular-season success.

The offseason's biggest splash came in late March when the Las Vegas Raiders sent two first-round picks to the New Orleans Saints in exchange for wide receiver Davante Adams, who restructured his contract to facilitate the deal. Adams, 33, told reporters he welcomed the change of scenery and expects to push the Raiders' offense into legitimate playoff contention alongside second-year quarterback Jaylen Covington. Saints head coach Dennis Allen, meanwhile, used the windfall of picks to rebuild a depleted defensive backfield, signing cornerbacks Tre Hernandez and Malik Pope to bolster a unit that surrendered 27 points per game last season.

Perhaps the most compelling storyline entering training camp involves the defending Super Bowl LX champion Kansas City Chiefs, who lost offensive coordinator Matt Nagy to the Chicago Bears head coaching vacancy in February. Patrick Mahomes addressed reporters Tuesday at the team's Arrowhead Stadium facility, expressing confidence in newly promoted coordinator Brian Dobrowski while acknowledging the adjustment period ahead. "Every year is a new puzzle," Mahomes said. "We've been through transitions before and found a way." Whether Kansas City can reload fast enough to chase a third consecutive championship remains the defining question of the 2026 offseason.
